# Pagination

```tsx
import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, PaginationRoot, PaginationSummary, getPaginationRange } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

Navigation between pages of content. Mirrors the Figma Pagination component: Type (Buttons / Simple) × Size (Small / Medium) × Page Count (≤ 7 / > 7) × Current Page (First / Mid / Last). Page Count and Current Page follow `pageCount` and `page`.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<Pagination
  {...args}
  onPageChange={(page) => {
    updateArgs({ page })
    onPageChange?.(page)
  }}
/>
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Pagination component: Type (Buttons / Simple) × Size (Small / Medium) × Page Count (≤ 7 / > 7) × Current Page (First / Mid / Last). `Pagination` builds the whole thing from `page` and `pageCount`; the parts below compose custom layouts.
- Buttons: Button Ghost arrows, .Pagination Button pages (Button Primary colors on the current one) and Pagination Ellipsis, 8px apart.
- Simple (Medium only): arrows around "Página 1 | 1 a 5 de 50 itens".

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`PaginationProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type?` | `"buttons" \| "simple"` | Figma Type. |
| `size?` | `PaginationSize` | Figma Size. Simple only exists in Medium. |
| `page` | `number` | The current page, starting at 1. |
| `getPageHref?` | `(page: number) => string` | Renders the pages as links instead of buttons. |
| `itemCount?` | `number` | Simple: total number of items. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Simple: items per page. |

`PaginationControlProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `href?` | `string` | Renders a link instead of a button. |

## Types

`PaginationProps`

## Rules

- Import `Pagination` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
